gaps.sentence: The ___ cost was much higher than the estimate.
gaps.explanation: 'Actual' means real or existing in fact; 'current' means belonging to the present time.

gaps.sentence: The ___ repairs were making the theatre impossible to run profitably.
I couldn't ___ what he was saying because of the noise.
gaps.explanation: 'Hear' means to receive sound; 'listen' means to pay attention deliberately and needs 'to'.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.
'Especially' means in particular or above all; 'specially' means for one particular purpose.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: The film was ___ good, but not brilliant.
gaps.hint: an adverb of degree is needed before 'good'
gaps.explanation: 'Quite' means fairly or rather; 'quiet' is an adjective meaning without noise.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its workers' wages by three per cent.
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' is transitive (raise wages); rise is intransitive.
